title: Quality finding
description:
One thing about a build that falls short of a bar, stated as work a specialist can do.

Every producer that judges a build - playability, production-quality, visual-qa, review, verification, listing-validation, a person at G4, and later the quality scorecard - reports its failures in its own shape. A quality finding is the one shape they are all normalized into, so that a finding can be routed to the discipline that owns it without a person translating it: the quality dimension it concerns, how severe it is, what was measured against which bar, the evidence, the owner discipline (a role in core/roles/roles.yaml), the concrete task (what to change, and how a re-measurement accepts it) and the route that takes it there (core/reference/specialist-routing.yaml).

A finding's `id` is stable across measurements of the same check by the same producer, which is what lets the gate that raised it say on the next build whether it was resolved.

`request` is what a person types at G4 (`wgf decide <run> iterate --findings FILE`): the dimension, severity, summary and task. The owner and the route are filled from the routing data, never guessed by the person.

dimension.description: The quality dimension a finding concerns. Each is owned by exactly one specialist (core/reference/specialist-routing.yaml `specialists`).

severity.description: blocker: the producer failed the build on it. major: a defect the producer saw that did not fail the build on its own. minor: polish.

route.description: Where the work is done: the game's code and content (develop, as the owning specialist), an asset made again (assets), the design revised - a scope or content increase the design must state first (design), or the store listing (listing).

change.description: What to change, in the build's terms.

acceptance.description: How the change is accepted: what the producer that raised the finding re-measures on the next build, or what the person who raised it checks at G4.

design_field.description: The game-design field a design-route finding concerns (e.g. build_spec.content).

producer.description: The artifact type the finding was read from (playability-report, production-quality-report, visual-qa-report, review-report, qa-report, listing-validation-report, decision-record), or `quality-scorecard`.

step.description: The workflow step that produced it.

check.description: The producer's own id for what failed: a check id, a VQA failed id (score:environment), a blocker id, a defect id.

project.description: The viewport (desktop, mobile) it was measured on, when the producer says.

request.description: A finding as a person states it at G4.

route.description: A person may ask for `design` (a scope or content increase the design must state first) or `assets` (an asset made again); otherwise the routing data decides.

id.description: <producer>:<check>[@<project>] - stable across measurements. A check the routing data splits by route (core/reference/specialist-routing.yaml `split`) is one finding per route: <producer>:<check>/<route>[@<project>].

measured.description: What the producer measured, as it reported it.

bar.description: The bar it was measured against, as the producer stated it.

evidence_refs.description: Frames, files and artifacts that show it: run-relative or absolute frame paths, repository paths, artifact ids.

owner.description: The specialist role (core/roles/roles.yaml) that owns the finding's dimension.

assets.description: Asset ids it concerns, when the producer names them.

measurement.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. For a producer that lists its checks (playability, production-quality, listing-validation): the measurement the finding was read from.

guarded_by.description: Since quality-report 1.2.0 / triage-report 1.2.0. The regression guards this failure already has: the lessons of core/reference/lessons.yaml whose check this finding's check is, with the tests that prove the check catches it. Empty or absent: no lesson names it, and a systemic cause is a lesson candidate.

excepted.description: The rule of the run's knowledge-contract this failure falls under is excepted by a person for this run (an active knowledge exception, core/artifacts/shared/knowledge-exception.schema.json): the triage lists the finding and does not route it. The producer's verdict is unchanged.

guard.description: A regression guard: the lesson (core/reference/lessons.yaml), the check that holds it (a check id of core/reference/check-tiers.yaml, `<source>:<id>`) and the tests that show the check catches it.

level.description: The rule's enforcement level in the run's knowledge-contract (derived from its checks' tiers).

lesson_candidate.description: Since quality-report 1.2.0 / triage-report 1.2.0. A systemic issue a specialist visit found: a class of defect the Factory let through, stated so it is true of any game, with the check that should hold it. Surfaced to the person deciding G4; promoted to core/reference/lessons.yaml (with a check and a test) or rejected by a person, never applied by itself.

summary.description: The lesson, generically: the root cause in the Factory, not this build's symptom.

root_cause.description: Why the Factory let it through: which gate, brief or step did not hold it.

proposed_check.description: The check that would hold it: an existing check id of core/reference/check-tiers.yaml to strengthen, or a new one to add.

finding.description: The quality finding id the visit was working when it saw it.

symptom.description: Added for knowledge ingestion (docs/knowledge-enforcement.md). What a player or a person saw on this build - the observation, kept apart from `summary` (the generalized lesson) and `root_cause` (the Factory's cause): symptom -> root cause -> systemic? -> candidate -> enforcement proposal.

systemic.description: Added for knowledge ingestion. Whether the reporter judges it a class of defect the Factory lets through (true) or this build's own mistake (false), and why. A candidate reported not systemic is stored, and never drafted into a lesson.

proposed_level.description: Added for knowledge ingestion. The enforcement level the reporter proposes. A proposal only: a level is derived from the tiers of the checks that hold a lesson, and a candidate whose evidence is subjective (a review's judgment, no measured finding) is never drafted as blocking or required.

proposed_scope.description: Added for knowledge ingestion. Where the reporter thinks it applies, in the vocabulary of a lesson's scope (core/reference/lessons.yaml): keys AND-ed, values OR-ed; empty is global.

proposed_checks.description: Added for knowledge model 2.1.0 (K5). Every check that would hold it, when it is held at more than one place (on the design and on the build); `proposed_check` is the first of them. The level is derived over all of them.

domain.description: Added for knowledge model 2.1.0 (K5). What part of a game the lesson is about (core/reference/lessons.yaml `domains`); promote drafts it on the lesson.

principle.description: Added for knowledge model 2.1.0 (K5). The reusable why, true of any game: X, because Y.

anti_pattern.description: Added for knowledge model 2.1.0 (K5). What violating it looks like, true of any game.

candidate_record.description: One entry of workspace/lessons/candidates.yaml (`wgf knowledge ingest`, scripts/wgf_knowledge/ingest.py): a lesson candidate collected from the run stores, de-duplicated, with every report it was seen in. Append-only: a later sighting adds a source; a person rejects one (`state: rejected`) or promotes it through a pull request that adds the lesson to core/reference/lessons.yaml (never this file, never automatically).

state.description: open, or rejected by a person (`wgf knowledge reject`). Promoted is not stored: it is read from workspace/lessons/evidence.yaml, whose lesson entry names the candidate it came from (`candidate`).

key.description: The de-duplication key: the normalized summary and the proposed check.

basis.description: Derived from the sources, never trusted as written. measured: at least one source from a measuring report resolved its finding to one the run's quality-report or triage-report recorded on the same build commit (a gate's check failed on that build); subjective: only judgments (a reviewer's comment, a person's or agent's opinion). A subjective candidate never becomes blocking or required by itself.

duplicate_of.description: A lesson that already names the proposed check but holds nothing yet (a candidate or gap lesson).

related_lessons.description: Active lessons that already hold the proposed check while this candidate states another problem (not a regression of them): a person decides whether it strengthens one of them or is a lesson of its own.

other_root_causes.description: Root causes other sources of the same candidate (same summary and check) gave, kept beside `root_cause` rather than dropped.

strength.description: Added for K6.4 (core/reference/evidence-strength.yaml, scripts/wgf_knowledge/strength.py). How far the measurements behind the candidate were repeated, derived from its sources' re-measurements in their runs' finding ledgers - never written by a reporter: hypothesis (no measured repair), single-run (one measured FAIL->PASS pair), reproduced (the pass repeated in a later independent measurement, on a stable check, by a class that is not only the game's own report), validated (reproduced in two or more distinct contexts, differing in run or commit: two scenarios of one run and build are one context). Promote derives it again from the run store; it caps the classification a draft may propose below REQUIRED.

strength_why.description: Added for K6.4. Why the strength is what it is: the pair, its repeats, the caps (unstable, self-reported, single-judge, unknown-class) and the refusals.

refused_evidence.description: Added for K6.4. Every measurement offered that may not count toward strength, with its rule and reason - never dropped silently: same-report (a), own-check (b), same-build (c), self-agreement (d), claim (e), duplicate, no-repair.

unstable.description: Added for K6.4. Findings whose check the ledger shows alternating verdicts (a pass, then a failure again; or a failure and a pass on one commit): a pair on them is capped at single-run.

candidate_source.description: Where a lesson candidate (or a regression observation) was seen: the run, the report by id, type, version and hash, the build commit, the reporter.

report_hash.description: The digest of the report file's bytes in the run store.

content_hash.description: The report's provenance content hash, when it carries one.

resolved_in.description: For a measured source: the measuring report (quality-report or triage-report) of the same run that recorded the finding on the same build - by id, version and the digest of its file - so promote can re-verify it against the run store. A source a promote cannot re-verify (run store gone, a digest that no longer matches, the finding absent) is subjective.

remeasurement.description: Added for K6.4. What the run's newest finding ledger (triage-report `lifecycle`) held of the source's finding when it was ingested (scripts/wgf_knowledge/strength.py snapshot): the ledger report, the finding, its producer, check and measurement class (core/reference/quality-assessment.yaml), the verification verdict, the before and after measurements (commit, content hash, seq, status, scenario, frame digests), the comparison, the samples, the detection and the outcomes history. Refreshed when the run is ingested again; promote reads it again from the run store and never trusts this copy.

build.description: The build a finding was measured on: its commit, and the digest of its bundle when verification built it (verification-report build_artifact.content_hash), else null.

measurement.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. One report's measurement of one check, as the ledger keeps it: the report, the commit it measured, the check and project, the status, and - for playability (playability-report 1.4.0) - the scenario the bot played for it and its frames. The `before` and `after` a repair is verified on.

seq.description: The report's run-local production order: with the content hash, which of two reports sharing an artifact id it was.

status.description: The check's status in that report (PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, SKIPPED, WARNING); null when the report does not list it.

scenario.description: The playability scenario: its id (`<check>@<project>`), the bot version and the settings it was handed, the viewport, the policy per recording and the seed. Null for a report that records none.

status.description: A finding's lifecycle. detected: a producer reported it. classified: its dimension, owner and route were decided from the routing data. assigned: a triage routed it to its owner. implemented: the owner's visit built a change for it. verified: the producer that raised it re-measured a newer build and it no longer fails, and nothing that was passing failed on that build (a fix that regresses another gate is not verified). closed: verified, and every gate the run holds a report of has measured the build carrying the fix. Never closed on the specialist's word: only on the raising gate's re-measurement - and, for a producer that lists its checks, only on a measurement of the same check on the same project (a check the report no longer lists, or lists as BLOCKED, SKIPPED or WARNING, verifies nothing; playability also needs another commit than the one it failed on). A verified or closed finding the gate raises again is classified again (reopened).

record.description: A finding in the run's lifecycle ledger (triage-report `lifecycle`): the finding as last measured, its status, every transition, and the verification evidence.

build.description: The build it was last observed failing on (the affected build).

expected.description: The threshold it is held to (the finding's bar).

observed.description: The value last measured (the finding's measured).

failed_measurement.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. The last measurement that failed the finding: the `before` its verification is compared with.

baseline.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. What the gates had measured when the finding was assigned (or, assigned by none, implemented): per producer, its newest report then, the commit, the findings it failed and - for a producer that lists its checks - the checks it passed (`<producer>:<check>[@<project>]`). A failure after the fix is a regression of it only when its check passed here, or it was verified before: a producer or check that had never measured raises a new finding, not a regression.

fix.description: The specialist visit that implemented it.

artifact_id.description: The artifact that made the change when no develop visit did: the assets step's asset-manifest, for a finding a gate routed straight to it.

verification.description: The raising producer's re-measurement of a newer build than the fix: its report, the build, what it measured, and any regressions that keep the finding from being verified.

verdict.description: passed: re-measured, no longer failing. still-failing: the producer still fails it (reopened). regressed: no longer failing, but the build fails what passed before. Since triage-report 1.3.0, for a producer that lists its checks, three that verify nothing and leave the finding open: unmeasured (the check is listed but measured nothing: BLOCKED, SKIPPED, WARNING or `measured.unmeasured`), missing (the report no longer lists the check for that project), same-build (playability passed it on the commit it failed on).

regressions.description: Findings first detected on a build at or after the fix: something that was passing fails now.

gates_measured.description: The producers whose reports measured a build at or after the fix.

before.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. The measurement that failed it.

after.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. The newer measurement the verdict was read from.

seq.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. The run-local seq of the report the verdict was read from.

samples.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. Every report of the raising producer that measured it passing, from the one that verified it on (the newest 20): one sample is a single run; more are the pass reproduced. Never a status of its own.

comparison.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. Whether `before` and `after` are the same scenario played by the same bot under the same settings on the same viewport, every difference named. A comparison with differences is weaker, and says so.

guarded_by.description: Since quality-report 1.2.0 / triage-report 1.2.0. The lessons whose check this finding's is (see finding.guarded_by).

detected_seq.description: Run-local order of the report it was first detected in.

by.description: The artifact or step the transition came from.

content_hash.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. The content hash of the artifact `by` names, when known: two reports can share an artifact id.

seq.description: Since triage-report 1.3.0. That artifact's run-local seq, when known.
